correctness.rationale: The coordinate proof is correct. The root halfspaces give P with support h_P(z)=max(||z||_infinity,||z||_1/2); every nonzero even-sum integer z satisfies h_P(z)<=||z||_2^2/2, while the roots already define P, hence P=V_D4. Polarity gives P*=C. The dual lattice is exactly the integral and all-half-integral cosets. For y in D4*, h_{C/2}(y) is half the sum of the two largest absolute coordinates; the integer and half-integral estimates each give h_{C/2}(y)<=||y||_2^2/2, and the shortest vectors already define C/2, so V_D4*=C/2. Codenotti--Freyer's open full text then supplies reducedness/completeness and scale invariance. The inspected exact-rational checker reconstructs both 24-vertex halfspace systems as corroboration.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality passes. The primary Codenotti--Freyer paper explicitly asks for an origin-symmetric simultaneous reduced-complete body in dimension at least three and notes that every higher-dimensional simultaneous example in its list is a simplex. Their polarity and Voronoi results are the needed general premises, but the inspected full text does not give a D4 or 24-cell instance. Resultary returned the assigned theorem as the exact D4 answer and no stronger prior SCOPE record. The nontrivial bridge is the same-lattice metric identity (V_D4)^*=2V_D4*.
residual_risks: The consequence is short once the D4 Voronoi duality is recognized, so an unindexed classical observation remains possible.
